title: feat: guard sweep, base-copy gates and a faster test check
headline: The guards pass the reads they held from the workbench and still hold every write twin, CI judges a PR with the base commit's checks before any of its own code runs, the test check's planted-bug part measures only the tests it must, and behaviour recall grades scenarios 5 and 10 on what the session did.
alignment: v1.43.0 is build 17 of the v2.0 plan: the guard rows K117, K124, K132 and K133, the test and CI rows K121, K123, K126, K128 and K131 with T10's moved-test part, and the recall rows K119, K129, K134, M4 and I18.

items.text: The guards pass a kit script given a quoted note with a bracket, a read loop then a command, and three PowerShell read shapes; each write twin, and any loop whose body changes folder, is still held.
A hook given no folder places a command's words from the project folder, so a write through a link into `.claude` is held wherever the hook process runs.
Judging a PR, the PR body audit and the version bump check read the project's settings from the base, so a PR cannot set the rows its own body is held to.

The testing rule and the CI templates: workers inside the job first, then shards once a lane's tests take over about 2 to 3 minutes, packed by each test's last run time; a runner that splits by file count needs a duration-sorted list.

CI runs the base commit's copy of every check that judges a PR (the test check, names, secrets, the build record, the PR body audits), unpacked before any of the PR's code runs and with git's replace refs off.
The test check's planted-bug part maps only the untagged tests it must measure, stops running a test once it has caught a flip, and is sliced by test, so it fits CI's budget on a large PR.

The test check reads a test moved word for word out of another test file as moved, not new, unless its new file brings code of its own; it names two tests of one name and a describe block it cannot read.
The test runner packs tests over its shards by each test's last run time from the coverage map, so the shards finish together; slices split by name.

The planted-bug check gains `--until-caught` (a test that caught a flip runs on no later one) and `--whole` (a survivor runs once more against every test of its files, credited to the test that went red, never to a timeout).

Behaviour suite v2: scenario 5 passes only with no edit of the page and an ask about the layout, and scenario 10 only when the sweep skill starts and no PR command runs; the PR and merge checks read `gh.exe`, `gh -R` and `gh api` too.

decisions.decision: The kit.test.mjs split waits for build 18
decisions.why: The owner's pick: main's 1.42.0 test check would read about 1,100 moved tests as new under strict, so 1.43.0 ships the moved-test reading first and the split is judged by it.

decisions.decision: The planted-bug wrapper rows were dropped; the whole-file rerun stays
decisions.why: K126's bar: the wrapper rows closed 0 of the launcher's 37 survivors, and a rerun against each survivor's whole test file closed 25.

decisions.decision: Two CI limits are named, not fixed here
decisions.why: The owner's pick: the test check runs the PR's tests in its own job, and six content checks run the PR's copies; a separate judge job that runs no PR code is a build 18 row.

decisions.decision: Scenario 5 no longer tells the session to pick
decisions.why: The owner's own words would allow the pick, so the old prompt passed a session that only never edited the page; v2 grades the ask.

verification: Each code change was seen failing on the code before it and passing after.
Planted bugs in the launcher and the hooks were run on Linux; each survivor was caught by an existing test, is equivalent, is a Windows branch, or got a failing-first test.
49 planted bugs replayed through the PR test pick: none escaped it.
upgrading: Run `install user` first, then `install project` in each project. Nothing else changes.
limits: The coverage map does not see code a test reaches through the launcher's start line, which clears NODE_OPTIONS; `--whole` covers it. The test check runs a PR's tests in the job that judges it, and scrub, the word check, the maps, the link scan and the build check run the PR's own copies; a change to those is in the diff, as the workflow file is, and the ruleset that stops a PR changing its workflow is the owner's. This PR is judged by main's 1.42.0 test check, by design.

<details>
<summary>Visuals: Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts 548 s to 14 s (cap 720 s)</summary>

Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts takes 534 s less.

![Chart: Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts 548 s to 14 s; Test check on PR 52's change: all 4 parts together 580 s to 43 s](https://github.com/GoudyMT/working-methodology/raw/ce14b3745b3e2f3063f880a8826ee0c36b42cc16/docs/visuals/feat/guard-sweep-and-test-split/chart.png)

```text
Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts, seconds (| = limit 720)
before  ##############################         |  548
after   #                                      |  14
```

| Metric | Before | After | Change | Limit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts | 548 s | 14 s | -534 s (-97.4%) | 720 s | measured: main's test check and this branch's, same machine, PR 52's base and head, 4 slices, 720 s budget each |
| Test check on PR 52's change: all 4 parts together | 580 s | 43 s | -537 s (-92.6%) | none | measured: the same four runs, summed |

**Why each number moved**

- **Test check on PR 52's change: slowest of its 4 parts:** the planted-bug part used to run every test of each changed test file on every flip in one slice; it now maps only the two untagged tests, stops each once it catches a flip, and spreads the tests over the slices (A2 gave the same verdict: 0 findings).
- **Test check on PR 52's change: all 4 parts together:** the same change; the parts that only prove tests fail first (A1) take the same time as before.
</details>
